title: The Flannan Isles Light (2)
subtitle: Outer Hebrides, 1900
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a remote Scottish island lighthouse station in the Outer Hebrides in December 1900, wet grey stone, heavy Atlantic sea, cold blue-grey storm light, melancholy and uncanny, cinematic composition, fine film grain. Single image, not a collage, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Scotland, December nineteen hundred. On a remote island in the Atlantic, the lighthouse went dark.
beats.img: Close view of the top of a tall stone lighthouse, its great glass lantern room completely dark and unlit, centred and large in frame against a churning grey storm sky at dusk.

beats.vo: Storms held the relief boat back until Boxing Day. When it finally landed, no one came down to meet it.
beats.img: A long empty stone stairway climbing steep wet black cliffs from a small concrete landing, an empty bare flagpole at the top, grey sea foam below, no boat, no figures.

beats.vo: The lamps had been cleaned and refilled. One man's oilskins were still inside. Investigators concluded he had gone out without them.
beats.img: A single dark oilskin coat hanging alone on an iron hook on a whitewashed stone wall inside a plain lighthouse passage, an empty row of hooks beside it, dim grey window light.

beats.vo: High on the west cliff, a box of ropes kept a hundred and ten feet above the sea had been smashed open.
beats.img: A narrow rock crevice high on a sheer wet sea cliff, splintered wooden planks and loose coiled rope scattered on the ledge, the grey Atlantic far below, spray in the air.

beats.vo: The inquiry blamed an unusually large wave. Not one of the three keepers was ever found.
beats.img: The empty lighthouse station seen from far out at sea in grey winter light, a small dark island under low cloud, the tower unlit, nothing moving.

facts.claim: Flannan Isles Lighthouse, Eilean Mòr, Outer Hebrides, Scotland; three keepers vanished December 1900
Steamer Archtor logged the light not lit on 15 December 1900; relief vessel Hesperus delayed by weather, reached the island 26 December (11 days)
On arrival no flag on the flagstaff, no provision boxes, none of the keepers there to meet them
Lamps cleaned and refilled / trimmed and ready
One set of oilskins left inside, suggesting one keeper went out without them
Muirhead's report: box of mooring/landing ropes kept in a crevice ~110 ft above sea level at the west landing had been washed away / broken and its contents strewn
Official conclusion: swept away by an unexpectedly large sea ('large roller'); no trace of the three men ever found
Still unexplained as of 2025-26; the dramatic logbook entries sometimes quoted are later fabrications (Mike Dash) and are NOT used here
